target_customer: Knowledge-work teams that use Chrome plus Slack and web apps (design, CRM, code review) and would adopt a shared browser
problem: Work is scattered across browser tabs and chat; teammates cannot easily share live app context or act on requests inline.
business_model: B2B SaaS per team (planned paid tier for shared passwords, team organization, SSO)

founders.name: Ron Bhattacharyay
previous_startups: Accounting startup that came out of YC and was sold (name not stated in the source)
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; Jimmy Liu's July 2025 post says he and Jimmy sold an earlier accounting startup. Education not found.

founders.name: Jimmy Liu
previous_startups: Accounting startup that came out of YC and was sold (name not stated in the source)
founders.background_notes: Wrote the browser engineering post; Chromium fork, React UI, WebRTC then SFU. Education not found.

founders.name: Sachin Kesiraju
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page as a founder; no bio found.

exit.reason: Founders wrote that they ran out of ideas to move Muddy forward and closed the project; people would not make a collaborative browser their default.

technical_complexity.rationale: A small team forked Chromium instead of using Electron, wrote a React tab UI and built streaming of shared tab DOM over WebRTC, later an SFU, which is demanding for four people.

defensibility.rationale: Value depended on whole teams switching, which is hard, but features such as shared tabs and chat could be copied and Chromium forks are common.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The founders named Chrome and Slack as the incumbents; users had small complaints but not enough to switch. No acquisition found.

market_need_then: Chrome and Slack were universal, with some tab overload and context switching complaints, but the founders report the pain was too mild to drive switching.

branding.domain_note: Used feelmuddy.com, not the exact .com; no source on how it was obtained.

rebrands.why: Product evolved from the multiplayer tab browser Sail to the chat plus browser Muddy; reason for the name not stated

branding.community_and_virality: Founder says the public launch reached number one on Hacker News; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand itself beyond a Hacker News launch; no evidence the name drove growth.

pivots.from: Sail, a browser with multiplayer tabs
pivots.to: Sail canvas with tabs, notes and images
pivots.why: First release was used mostly as a meeting tool, not a default browser

pivots.to: Muddy, a browser combined with chat
pivots.why: Canvas was too complicated and niche; aim to replace Slack and Chrome

outcome_analysis: Muddy tried to replace both Chrome and Slack with a shared browser. The founders wrote in July 2025 that users would not adopt a collaborative browser as their default, complaints about incumbents were too small, always-on multiplayer made people uneasy, and heavy users wanted it alone. After two pivots from Sail and about $5.5 million reported raised, they closed the project. Pivot dates are approximate.
notes: The $5.5M seed and investor list rest on one secondary outlet (pulse.bot, summarizing the founders' Notion page); date unknown. CB Insights shows only a round with YC and no amount. The YC batch is S19 and founded 2018 per YC, but the founders' write-up and Latka date the browser work to 2020, so the S19 idea may have differed; unresolved. The website is still live with a 2024 footer. Competitors left empty: the only dated rival found (Sidekick) launched in 2021, too late for the 2019 batch. A Launch HN post exists but its date could not be verified.
